scores.visual_critic_note: Intentional Paul Tol palette and thoughtful node-state encoding (open circle = expanded, filled = collapsed, rank-colored) lift it above generic, but the lower half of the viewport is entirely wasted empty space, and collapsed Phylum nodes use the same pink (#EE6677) as search-match highlights, making the two states visually indistinguishable.
scores.encoding_integrity_note: Topological tree has no quantitative channels to deceive; categorical color correctly encodes rank; circle size is fixed (not data-driven), so no lie factor; only mild concern is the name+depth composite key instead of a stable unique ID, which could corrupt joins on data with duplicate names.
scores.stress_test_note: No .interrupt() call before new transitions in update(), so rapid clicks or Expand/Collapse All during a 500ms animation will queue rather than interrupt, causing positional snapping; all other checks pass—search is debounced at 200ms, pointer events unify mouse/touch, no brush/zoom storms, and no cross-view dispatch loops.
scores.cognitive_load_note: Progressive disclosure keeps the default 2-level view uncluttered and immediately readable; 6-rank color palette is within limits, search+count badges handle the 200-node depth well, though full-expansion density and simultaneous animation across all nodes can't be fully assessed from a static screenshot.
